judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the photo on the fourth news card. It is not inside a link. It shows the Polícia Civil MT badge on the front of the Polícia Judiciária Civil building, and its alt is "Imagem referente a notícia 4". Strictly, the claim is not true as worded: the alt describes no scene at all, so it cannot describe something the image does not show. It is a generic numbered placeholder. The element fails 1.1.1 under F30, which covers placeholder text used as an alternative. If the photo is informative, the alt conveys none of it. If it is decorative, a non-empty alt stops assistive technology from ignoring it. Read in good faith, the claim points at that defect, as the rubric's example allows. The live JS bundle still builds this alt as `Imagem referente a notícia ${e+1}`, and the styled screenshot matches, so the capture does not differ.

judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: The element is the inline SVG logo in the footer (class "logo", g id "logo-portalmtgovbr"), showing the words "MT.gov.br". It has no title, aria-label or role, and no aria-hidden. The snapshot exposes it as an image with no name, so assistive technology gets nothing from it. That is the sense in which the claim calls it hidden: it is not aria-hidden. No text on the page says "MT.gov.br", so the claim holds of the capture. My lean is that it fails 1.1.1: W3C guidance treats a logotype as informative, with the logo's text as its alternative. The other side is reasonable, though. The logo sits beside the text "GOVERNO DO ESTADO DE MATO GROSSO", so some auditors would call it redundant and decorative, and an unnamed SVG with no role is usually skipped by screen readers. Since competent auditors could disagree, the label is uncertain. The live bundle renders the same unnamed svg.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the footer link "MT Cidadão", href /#produtos-digitais. On this page that anchor is the 'Produtos Digitais' section. Its first item presents the MT Cidadão app: a heading, a paragraph that starts "O MT Cidadão é um aplicativo...", and links "Baixar MT Cidadão na Google Play/App Store". Rampa seems to have had only the section heading 'Produtos Digitais', not the content that shows the section is about this app, so the cause is context_missing. The live bundle has the same footer item {title:"MT Cidadão",href:"/#produtos-digitais"} and the same section.
